ABSTRACT: Confinement of hydrocarbons in nanoscale pockets and pores provides tunable capability for controlling molecules in catalysts, sorbents, and membranes for reaction and separation applications. While computation of the enthalpic interactions of hydrocarbons in confined spaces has improved, understanding and predicting the entropy of confined molecules remains a challenge. Here we show, using a set of nine aluminosilicate zeolite frameworks with broad variation in pore and cavity structure, that the entropy of adsorption can be predicted as a linear combination of rotational and translational entropy. The extent of entropy lost upon adsorption is predicted using only a single material descriptor, the occupiable volume ( $ V_{occ} $). Predictive capability of confined molecular entropy permits an understanding of the relation with adsorption enthalpy, the ability to computationally screen microporous materials, and an understanding of the role of confinement on the kinetics of molecules in confined spaces.

On the basis of this shape-selective feature , highly effective molecular separations and selective catalytic conversions can be achieved within zeolitic structures that are difficult to accomplish with other materials and/or techniques . $ ^ { 1-3 } $ So far, several shape-selectivity mechanisms have been elucidated and applications identified. $ ^{2-18} $ In common molecular sieving, bulky molecules adsorb preferentially over bulkier species as a result of steric constraints imposed by the zeolites' framework, e.g., linear alkane molecules compared to branched isomers. $ ^{19-23} $ Besides this common adsorption competition based on molecular bulkiness, the reverse phenomenon can also occur, i.e., competitive adsorption in favor of the bulkier species. The enthalpy and the entropy contributions to the Gibbs free energies were calculated at T = 298 K and partial pressure of 1 atm (101325 Pa). The enthalpy (H) of gas-phase pyridine and acetonitrile molecules is defined as the sum of total electronic energy ( $ E_{el} $), internal vibrational energy ( $ E_{v} $), zero-point vibrational energy (ZPVE), as well as the rotational and translational contributions to the internal energy: $ H = E_{el} + E_{v} + ZPVE + E_{R} + E_{t} $. The corresponding calculated entropies (S) includes translational, ( $ S_{t} $) vibrational, ( $ S_{v} $) and rotational ( $ S_{r} $) degrees of freedom: $ S = S_{t} + S_{v} + S_{r} $. All the considered systems are in singlet state, thus the electronic contribution to the entropy is zero. Since both adsorbed molecules are constrained in the zeolite cavity their entropy contributions in the adsorption complexes were corrected as follows: the translational and rotational degrees of freedom were reduced by 1 and 1.28 [37]. The first attempts to describe guest-induced flexibility in zeolites were done using molecular dynamics simulations. $ ^{79-82} $ Rigid zeolitic force fields were dynamically modified using transition state theory to include lattice flexibility, and the results obtained by these models were in good agreement with experimental data. $ ^{79-81,83,84} $ It was shown that framework flexibility in silicalite-1 (MFI-type framework) is responsible for the adsorption of large molecules such as isobutane and heptane with inflection behavior at high loadings, $ ^{80} $ while enhanced self-diffusivity at low loadings of short alkanes (i.e. methane and n-butane) was observed. $ ^{81} $ Framework flexibility is also crucial for aromatics adsorption on MFI zeolite, especially at high pressures. $ ^{84,85} $ While the use of rigid zeolitic models led to the underestimation of the aromatics adsorption in MFI zeolite by a factor of two, $ ^{84,85} $ the use of flexible models to simulate diffusion coefficients of various alkanes in silicalite-1 zeolite resulted in a convergence of experimental and theoretical values. $ ^{86} $ Recently by using in situ integrated differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy (iDPC-STEM) while adsorbing benzene molecules on MFI zeolite, Xiong et al. showed that the MFI structure goes through severe deformations giving another proof of guest-induced flexibility in zeolites (see Fig. 4). $ ^{87} $

2.4.4. Trapdoor. Traditional diﬀusion models primarily consider two types of interactions: those between guest molecules (guest–guest) and those between guest molecules and the zeolite framework (guest–host). However, when cations are present in the zeolite structure, a third interaction—involving guest molecules, the framework, and cations (guest–host-cation)—must also be accounted for. A striking example of such ternary interactions is the well-known ‘‘molecular trapdoor’’. This phenomenon, also referred to as the ‘‘gating effect’’, describes a unique molecular sieving mechanism in certain zeolites and related porous materi- als. Here, extra-framework cations function as dynamic gate- keepers at pore apertures, selectively controlling molecular diffusion to achieve highly discriminative adsorption and separation.9,147,187 To date, ‘‘trapdoor’’ has been observed in several zeolites, including RHO (DNL-6),188–190 CHA (SAPO-34, SSZ-13),147,191,192 MWF (ZSM-25),149,193 HEU (Clinoptilolite),194

descriptor_candidates.name: conf_shape_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss (normalized by R) increases with the ratio of occupiable pore volume per mass (AV) to molecular volume (Vol), because tighter fit (smaller AV/Vol) imposes stronger translational/rotational confinement; adding this ratio as a 15th network input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas prediction versus the 14-input baseline.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Confinement entropy loss scales with the mismatch between accessible pore volume and molecular volume: a molecule filling its pore loses nearly all translational freedom (Sackur-Tetrode limit), while in large cavities it retains partial freedom. Inference from E01/E03, which show entropy loss varies by framework and correlates with occupiable volume; the ratio makes the molecule-size dependence explicit and nonlinear rather than leaving it to the network.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If 10-fold cross-validated MAE with AV/Vol added does not improve on the 14-input baseline MAE (or degrades it), or if residuals show no correlation with AV/Vol, the hypothesis is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: asymmetry_confinement_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss grows with a combined index coupling molecular anisotropy (SPAN/GeDi) to the gap between molecular volume and pore-bounding sphere (PBF^3): elongated, shape-mismatched molecules lose more entropy under confinement than compact molecules of equal Vol, because rotational degrees of freedom are frozen out preferentially in narrow channels.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: E01 notes rotational plus translational fractions of gas-phase entropy determine adsorbed entropy; E09 shows molecular symmetry strongly affects mobility under confinement. Inference: rotational entropy loss depends on molecular anisotropy relative to channel geometry, captured here by shape descriptors (SPAN, GeDi, PBF, Vol) rather than volume alone.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If adding this index does not reduce MAE relative to baseline, or if the improvement disappears when AV (pore volume) alone is controlled for (i.e., anisotropy adds no information beyond pore size), the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_vicinity_factor
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases with a surface-vicinity factor combining molecular surface-to-volume ratio (LabuteASA/Vol, proxy for contact area with pore walls) and framework density: molecules with high wall-contact area in dense frameworks (small lsd_p, high density) behave closer to immobile adsorbates, losing roughly the full 3D translational entropy, while low-contact molecules in large cavities retain more.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: E01 states immobile adsorbates lose entropy equal to full 3D translation; wall contact area governs the transition from mobile to immobile adsorption. Framework density at its source numerical scale (no unverified units, per task rules) and pore-limiting diameter lsd_p modulate steric hindrance. Inference: entropy loss is a smooth saturating function of contact-area density, distinct from pure free-volume arguments.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE with this factor added does not beat the 14-input baseline, or if the factor's contribution is not statistically distinguishable from noise across cross-validation folds, the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: aperture_free_volume_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss (in units of R) increases when the pore-limiting aperture lsd_p is small relative to the free-volume-per-contact-area ratio (AV*ASA/Vol): narrow apertures relative to cavity volume trap molecules in vibration-like states, freezing translational and rotational degrees of freedom, so adding log(AV*ASA/(Vol*lsd_p)) as a 15th network input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas versus the 14-input baseline.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01, which shows entropy loss differs strongly by framework (TON largest, FAU smallest) and is governed by translational/rotational freedom, and from E05, which shows pore aperture size imposes steric constraints. Mechanism: the descriptor couples three confinement controls — free volume per mass (AV), wall area (ASA), molecular size (Vol) and the narrowest passage (lsd_p) — capturing aperture-limited cages that free-volume arguments alone miss. Source evidence establishes V_occ as a predictor; the explicit aperture/free-volume product is an inferred combination.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If 10-fold cross-validated MAE with this descriptor added does not improve on the retained-round baseline MAE of 0.5431 (in R units), or if its SHAP/permutation importance is indistinguishable from noise across folds, the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: asphericity_size_factor
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss grows with molecular asphericity (PMI3/PMI1 ratio) scaled by the ratio of molecular span to pore-limiting diameter: elongated molecules in apertures comparable to their longest dimension lose rotational entropy preferentially, so adding sqrt(PMI3/PMI1)*(SPAN/lsd_p) as a 15th input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas beyond the baseline plus AV/Vol.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 (rotational entropy fraction governs adsorbed entropy and its confinement loss) and E09 (molecular symmetry controls mobility under confinement). Mechanism: a prolate molecule (PMI3 >> PMI1) whose span approaches lsd_p can translate only by alignment with the channel, freezing two rotational degrees of freedom — a shape effect absent from purely volumetric descriptors. All terms are dimensionless ratios, avoiding unit-scale issues.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE does not improve over the round-2 retained baseline (0.5431), or if residuals show no dependence on the descriptor after controlling for AV/Vol, the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: packing_tightness_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss saturates with a packing-tightness factor: when molecular volume approaches the product of pore volume and limiting diameter (Vol/(AV*lsd_p) -> 1), the molecule is nearly jammed and behaves as an immobile adsorbate losing the full 3D translational entropy (~Sackur-Tetrode), while the surface-to-volume term (LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3)) weights how much wall contact enforces immobilization; adding this factor as a 15th input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01, which states immobile adsorbates lose entropy equal to three translational degrees of freedom and that confinement loss is framework-specific. Mechanism: a smooth saturating function of free-space mismatch distinguishes the mobile-to-immobile transition, with the contact-area term encoding how much of the molecular surface is constrained by walls. Distinct from round-1 surface_vicinity_factor by using the squared free-space mismatch and explicit surface-to-volume geometry rather than an exponential of contact density alone.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If cross-validated MAE with this factor added does not beat the 0.5431 baseline, or if the exponential packing term contributes no significant information (permutation test p > 0.05 across folds), the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: wall_curvature_aperture_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss (normalized by R) increases with the dimensionless wall-curvature index (ASA * lsd_p / AV): frameworks with large wall area per occupiable volume (ASA/AV, an inverse pore-radius proxy) and small limiting apertures (lsd_p) confine molecules in narrow, high-curvature channels where translational freedom approaches the immobile-adsorbate limit; adding this index as a 15th network input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas versus the retained 14+AV/Vol baseline.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 (entropy loss is framework-specific, largest in TON-type small-channel frameworks, and equals full 3D translational loss for immobile adsorbates) and E05 (aperture-imposed steric constraints determine adsorption state). Mechanism: ASA/AV measures how much pore wall exists per unit free volume (a curvature/space-filling measure), and multiplying by lsd_p makes it dimensionless and aperture-weighted — distinguishing narrow channels from large cavities at equal free volume, information the volumetric AV/Vol ratio alone cannot encode.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If 10-fold cross-validated MAE does not improve on the 0.5431 (R units) retained baseline, or if permutation importance of the descriptor is indistinguishable from noise after controlling for AV/Vol, the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: cage_aperture_shape_contrast
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss decreases with cage-aperture shape contrast ((lsd_f - lsd_p)/GeDi, cage-like expansion) weighted by molecular compactness (PMI1/PMI3): molecules in large-cavity frameworks (large lsd_f - lsd_p) that are near-spherical (PMI3 ≈ PMI1) retain most rotational freedom and lose little entropy, whereas elongated molecules (small PMI1/PMI3) lose rotational entropy even in cages; adding this contrast term as a 15th input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 (rotational plus translational fractions govern adsorbed entropy; FAU cages show the smallest loss) and E09 (molecular symmetry and shape control mobility under confinement). Mechanism: the free-space expansion between the limiting aperture and the largest free sphere (lsd_f - lsd_p) indicates cage-like versus channel-like topology; its interaction with molecular asphericity captures the shape-dependent rotational freezing that pure volume or aperture descriptors miss, making the network's shape–topology interaction explicit.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If adding the descriptor does not reduce cross-validated MAE below 0.5431, or if the improvement vanishes when AV/Vol and lsd terms are controlled for (no residual dependence on the contrast index), the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 (immobile adsorbates lose entropy equal to three translational degrees of freedom via Sackur–Tetrode; loss is framework-dependent) and E06 (confined molecules retain only a reduced fraction of translational/rotational entropy). descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If cross-validated MAE does not improve on the 0.5431 baseline, or if the exponential saturation term contributes no significant information across folds (permutation test p > 0.05), the hypothesis is falsified.

candidates.name: contact_immobilization_saturation
candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss saturates with a contact-immobilization factor: the exponential free-space term exp(-Vol/(AV*lsd_p)) decays as the molecule fills the accessible volume (Vol → AV*lsd_p), driving the adsorbate toward the immobile limit of full 3D translational entropy loss, while the specific surface term (LabuteASA/Vol) scales the fraction of molecular surface in wall contact that freezes rotations; adding this product as a 15th input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas.
candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 (immobile adsorbates lose entropy equal to three translational degrees of freedom via Sackur–Tetrode; loss is framework-dependent) and E06 (confined molecules retain only a reduced fraction of translational/rotational entropy). Mechanism: the factor models a smooth mobile-to-immobile transition — distinct from the rejected round-2 squared packing term by using a linear-exponent saturation and specific-surface (LabuteASA/Vol) rather than surface-to-volume^(2/3) weighting, so it encodes both jamming and wall-contact area monotonically and finitely for all positive inputs.
candidates.falsification_criteria: If cross-validated MAE does not improve on the 0.5431 baseline, or if the exponential saturation term contributes no significant information across folds (permutation test p > 0.05), the hypothesis is falsified.

interpretation: Replicates vary LLM proposals on one fixed split, not independent datasets. Novelty is unverified.

retained.name: conf_shape_ratio
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss (normalized by R) increases with the ratio of occupiable pore volume per mass (AV) to molecular volume (Vol), because tighter fit (smaller AV/Vol) imposes stronger translational/rotational confinement; adding this ratio as a 15th network input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas prediction versus the 14-input baseline.

retained.name: wall_curvature_aperture_index
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss (normalized by R) increases with the dimensionless wall-curvature index (ASA * lsd_p / AV): frameworks with large wall area per occupiable volume (ASA/AV, an inverse pore-radius proxy) and small limiting apertures (lsd_p) confine molecules in narrow, high-curvature channels where translational freedom approaches the immobile-adsorbate limit; adding this index as a 15th network input lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas versus the retained 14+AV/Vol baseline.
